head: c0a7bd9fd6e19cc40af3dcfed83b8fa20d8401c3
classification_reasons: Spec is tight (all five intent open questions answered, both Flagged concerns closed with a stated decision, acceptance measurable by grep/link-resolution), but blast radius is not small: the plan's own 'Files that change' lists ~23 new docs/notes/ files, 26 new docs/decisions/ files, 14 new docs/progress/ files, 3 new index.md files, 2 rewritten stubs and edits to 4 live docs (HANDOFF.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, README.md) plus a new docs/PROGRESS.md entry -- around 70 file touches once phase (c) runs, which is not 'few files' under the build guide's routine test.

No risk_list item and no schema/contract change (confirmed: no plugin/ or template/ file in scope, verified against sdlc.yaml risk_list), and no code is touched so the third routine criterion (code already covered by existing tests) is not applicable rather than satisfied -- the change is pure documentation restructuring with no test harness covering it either way.

The design itself is deferred: phase (c) will run against whatever docs/NOTES.md, docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/PROGRESS.md contain after sessions 15-16 append to them, so the exact file count/slugs are not fixed yet (plan.md Risks, 'Most of this is not implementable from this plan alone yet, by design') -- another reason to keep the tighter non-routine gate for the eventual build.
attempted: Intent: compared spec.md/plan.md against intent.md's Proposed outcome, Constraints and the five settled Open questions -- every proposed-outcome bullet (notes/decisions/progress split, frontmatter fields, stubs, four-doc link update, CLAUDE.md table handoff, timing hold until after v1.0.0) is carried through into spec.md Requirements/Design and plan.md Files-that-change/Order-of-work with no drift toward a different problem.

Spec and plan: verified the three Flagged concerns in spec.md each carry a decision (MODEL_ALLOCATION.md left out of scope; slug derivation left to a build-time mechanical pass per plan.md's 'Files that change'; index ordering taken as number order) -- none is left open. Cross-checked plan.md's Order of work against spec.md's Design section; the two agree on sequence (notes, then decisions, then progress, then the four live docs, then build/test/lint, then the owner's PROGRESS entry). No code diff exists yet to check against plan.md's file list/order (that check applies at phase (c), when the actual moves land).

Proof: this is phase (b); plugin/gate/artifacts.py's REQUIRED_EVIDENCE has no entry for phase 'b' (only REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS: intent.md, spec.md, plan.md), so the absence of test.log/build.log/lint.log/verifier.md in evidence/ is correct, not a gap -- no toolchain evidence was owed at this phase, and none is claimed in spec.md/plan.md's Proof section beyond 'will be collected' language that correctly defers proof to phase (c)/(d).

Blast radius: the actual diff-b.patch only touches changes/0001-.../spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml and evidence/ (hook-log.jsonl, run-b.json) -- no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) and nothing under plugin/ or template/ is in this diff. Used Grep to independently verify the factual claims spec.md/plan.md make about the live repo: docs/NOTES.md has exactly 23 '## ' sections, docs/DECISIONS.md has exactly 26 '## N.' decisions, docs/PROGRESS.md has 15 top-level '# ' records (1 current + 14 archived) -- all match the counts the spec and plan state, so the design's factual basis is not an unverified claim.

Policies: security-baseline and data-conventions are addressed with a specific rationale (moved text is pre-existing non-secret platform facts/decisions/records, nothing new introduced); ux-conventions is explicitly marked not-applicable with a reason (no user-facing surface); risk_list is explicitly checked against sdlc.yaml's four items and none applies. None of the five skills is silently skipped.

Tests: change_type is 'feature', not 'fix', so the test-file-lock rule does not apply; no file under tests/ is touched by this diff and none is planned to change in phase (c) either (plan.md Proof: 'no new test is added by this change'), so there is nothing to check for weakened pre-existing tests.

Checked for internal inconsistency: found one minor, non-blocking date discrepancy -- intent.md's Open Questions header says the five questions were settled with the owner 'on 2026-10-02 (PR #86)', while spec.md's 'Open questions from intent' section says 'settled on 2026-09-02 (PR #86)'. Same PR, different date; does not affect any requirement, acceptance criterion or file list, and does not meet REVIEW.md's bar for Important (would break behavior, leak data or breach a policy), so it is not raised as an escalation reason, only noted here.
